{{Quote|So your orders were to hold your position on the far side, and you didn't abandon your post until last month, even though you didn't receive a single transmission in over a year.|A Rebel trooper to the scout trooper|<ref name="Marooned" />}}
This '''particular clone [[Scout trooper/Legends|scout trooper]]''' was part of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] unit, assigned to guarding the [[Endor shield generator bunker]], [[Tempest Force/Legends|Tempest Force]]. The scout trooper was given the task of holding his position on the far side of the [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] while stationed there. After a year of not receiving any transmissions, he finally left his post, and met a [[Rebel trooper/Legends|Rebel trooper]] who had been left on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], learning that the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] had beaten the Empire at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].

==Biography==
===Marooned on Endor===
{{Quote|So, they left you behind too, huh?|An unidentified Rebel trooper to an unidentified scout trooper|<ref name="Marooned" />}}
This unidentified scout trooper was born sometime prior to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] in one of the clone factories. His genetic code was based on the phenotype of Jango Fett. He joined the [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]] and became a scout trooper. Like other troopers, he was "bred to take orders," without any hopes or ideals, only mental conditioning.<ref name="Marooned" />

In 4 ABY, the scout trooper was part of a group of Imperials selected to guard the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II's]] shield generator, Tempest Force. At some point prior to the Battle of Endor, him and his squad were assigned to the far side of the moon, after which, they never received any more orders from their superiors. Unbeknownst to them, the Rebels had won the battle and the Empire had retreated from the moon.<ref name="Marooned" />

Over the next twelve [[Standard month/Legends|months]] the trooper's squad-mates began began to die, leaving an impact on the scout trooper and causing him to finally abandon his position in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]]. One month later, the trooper was riding his [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]] when its battery died. He soon encountered a [[Unidentified Rebel trooper (Endor)|Rebel trooper]] who had also been left behind. The two fought for 45 minutes before they agreed on a truce, though they hardly got along in any friendly capacity. The scout trooper threatened to bring the Rebel trooper in as his prisoner, only when he attempted to subdue the Rebel, he brought not only the Rebel, but himself into a trap created by the native [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]].<ref name="Marooned" />

The Ewoks eventually came back to their trap, tying the scout trooper to a log and giving the Rebel trooper food. The scout trooper demanded that the Rebel trooper talk the Ewoks into releasing him upon return to their village, which he did. After being released, they were both given a peace pipe and the scout trooper told the Rebel his history and how he was bred to follow orders, after which, the Rebel told him his. The scout trooper then pulled out a drawing of the Death Star's shield generator, showing it to the Ewoks and asking them to take him there.<ref name="Marooned" />

The Ewoks led the scout trooper and the Rebel to the location of the shield generator, where they discovered that it had been destroyed and that the Rebels had won the battle. Resigned to being stuck on Endor, the scout trooper nearly gave up, but the Rebel trooper spotted an abandoned [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|AT-ST]]. While the pair checked the leftover vehicle's power cells, a [[Gorax/Legends|Gorax]] attacked the Ewoks that had been leading them. The Rebel trooper used the walker's cannons to kill the beast, much to the chagrin of the scout trooper, who wanted to keep the energy in the power cells. The Rebel trooper then picked up a structure on the walker's radar, about the size of a small city and transmitting an Imperial code.<ref name="Marooned" />

===Getting Off Endor===
{{Quote|Look on the brightside...this means finally getting out of here.''"<br />"''Yeah, as your ''frelling prisoner''. At least here, when I was alone, I was a ''free man''.''"<br />"''Okay, tell you what&mdash;as soon as I get back to my regiment, I'll find a way to get you off this rock. How does that sound?|An unidentified scout trooper and an unidentified Rebel trooper|<ref name="Marooned" />}}
When they arrived at the location of the signal, they discovered that it wasn't a city, but rather a [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] that had plummeted to the moon during the battle. The ship had a communication's substation and an operational power plant, and the Rebel trooper managed to contact a passing freighter on a nearby trade route. He also discovered that the signal was an automatic evacuation signal.<ref name="Marooned" />

The next morning, the freighter arrived. The scout trooper, however, decided to stay behind, citing that the Rebel trooper, who had previously said that people like him didn't have a place in peaceful society, was right. The two shook hands and said farewell, and the Rebel trooper boarded the freighter.<ref name="Marooned" />

The scout trooper later grew out his hair and watched the moon's sunsets from on top of an AT-ST.<ref name="Marooned" />

==Behind the scenes==
This trooper was never given a name, though the Rebel trooper refers to him as "Egg Man" throughout the story. The trooper also uses the curse word "[[Frell (expletive)|frell]]," from the television series, [[Wikipedia:Farscape|''Farscape'']].
